ringOnly.name: Dettifoss
ringOnly.why: Europe's most powerful waterfall by volume. Its access roads shut early in the season.

ringOnly.name: Stokksnes / Vestrahorn
ringOnly.why: Vestrahorn's jagged peaks over black dunes — arguably the most dramatic single landscape either plan can reach.

ringOnly.name: Goðafoss
ringOnly.why: The waterfall of the gods — a wide horseshoe right beside Route 1.

ringOnly.name: Akureyri
ringOnly.why: Iceland's northern capital — proper restaurants, a botanical garden, the last real town before the west.

ringOnly.name: Borgarnes
ringOnly.why: Settlement Centre if it's still open; otherwise the pool.

ringOnly.name: Dimmuborgir
ringOnly.why: Eleven minutes from the Mývatn bed. Doable on arrival or as an evening walk.

ringOnly.name: Djúpivogur
ringOnly.why: East-fjord village and the Eggin í Gleðivík eggs, on the emptiest tarmac of the trip.

ringOnly.name: Grjotagja
ringOnly.why: Seven minutes from the Myvatn bed.

ringOnly.name: Hvalnes headland
ringOnly.why: Black-sand spit under a scree mountain, on Route 1 between Djupivogur and Stokksnes. Four minutes of driving.

ringOnly.name: Hverir (Námaskarð)
ringOnly.why: Pin is the Route 1 layby, not the field — the obvious coordinate snaps to a footpath and OSRM then charges 34 phantom minutes. From the layby it is free: it sits exactly where the…

ringOnly.name: Petra's Stone Collection
ringOnly.why: A lifetime's mineral collection filling a house and garden in Stodvarfjordur. Private — confirm October opening by phone.

ringOnly.name: Skutustadagigar
ringOnly.why: Pseudocraters on the Myvatn south shore — on the road in from Godafoss, not a detour.

ringOnly.name: Víkurfjara beach
ringOnly.why: Vík's own black beach, straight off the village — the same black sand and surf as Reynisfjara but without the crowds or the sneaker-wave headland.

ringOnly.name: Ásbyrgi
ringOnly.why: Top-20 #19. A horseshoe canyon 100 m deep, said to be Sleipnir's hoofprint. Reachable only because you sleep at Mývatn and can cut its daytime dwell.

oursOnly.name: Kirkjufell & Kirkjufellsfoss
oursOnly.why: The most photographed mountain in Iceland, with its waterfall in front.

oursOnly.name: Arnarstapi cliffs
oursOnly.why: Sea arches, basalt columns and the cliff path to Hellnar.

oursOnly.name: Brimketill lava pool
oursOnly.why: A lava rock pool cut into the coast by the sea.

oursOnly.name: Búðakirkja black church
oursOnly.why: A black timber church standing alone in a lava field.

oursOnly.name: Djúpalónssandur
oursOnly.why: Black pebble beach with the ribs of a 1948 trawler still lying on it.

oursOnly.name: Fjallsárlón
oursOnly.why: Quieter lagoon, glacier tongue up close

oursOnly.name: Gerðuberg basalt cliffs
oursOnly.why: A long wall of hexagonal basalt columns.

oursOnly.name: Gunnuhver hot springs
oursOnly.why: Steam vents and a boiling mud pool on Reykjanes.

oursOnly.name: Krýsuvík / Seltún
oursOnly.why: Seltún's boiling mud flats and sulphur colours.

oursOnly.name: Lóndrangar sea pinnacles
oursOnly.why: Basalt sea pinnacles standing off the cliffs.

oursOnly.name: Rauðfeldsgjá gorge
oursOnly.why: A narrow gorge you walk up into, with water underfoot.

oursOnly.name: Reykjadalur hot river
oursOnly.why: A hot river you hike 3 km up to, then sit in.

oursOnly.name: Reykjanesviti
oursOnly.why: Iceland's oldest lighthouse, on the southwest tip.
